title: mcp/list_sufficient_sets/v4
description: v4 (2026-10-21, F09-T76; D-25, D-28 v3.46): a route settles either way. Each set carries `settles` — `proves` (the root's own routes, its direct proof, a resolves variant: the sets of v3.40) or `refutes` (a set closing a refutes variant, D-30 v3.46, enumerated from that variant's routes exactly as the root's are from its own; `variant` names it). A set's id is unchanged (its statements and assemblies), so every proving id stays. Order: the proving sets first in the record's order, then the refuting ones; a refuting set is never dropped as dominated by a proving one or the other way round, and the cap counts both sides. A proved root has no refuting sets; a refuted root no sets. Each selector node carries `side`: when sets of both sides exist the tree opens on a fork — the top node splits on no statement (route, node and set null) and has exactly two children, the proving family (`side: proves`) then the refuting one (`side: refutes`), each the selector of its own sets alone; `side` is null on every other node, and everywhere when one side only (then the tree is v3's). A false member of a set never refutes the root: it kills its route, no more. v3 (2026-10-19, F27-T9, R13): the result carries `at_proved`, what the enumeration did at a proved statement — `stop` (the default, F27-R5: a closed member, nothing beneath it listed) or `follow` (the statement expanded along what its first proof's term rests on, F18-R2, transitively, so the set also lists the proved structure it already stands on) — and each set `proof_routes`, the routes those proofs went through (every hole of the route among what its node's proof used), empty under `stop`. The sets are the same under both: the same ids, open statements, assemblies, routes and order, because the cut is still made at the proved statement; `follow` only adds what lies beneath. v2 (2026-10-17, F29-T4, R8; D-25, D-28 v3.44): each route carries `approach`, the one-line attack its partial declares (graph.json's decompositions[].approach, F29-R4), each hole its node's `label` (graph.json's label, F29-R3), and the result carries `selector`, the tree of route choices over the sets (opn_gate.routes.selector_tree, F29-R6): split, in record order, on the first statement on which the sets choose different routes, one child per route, recursively; every leaf is one set and every set one leaf; an interior node names the statement split on and counts the sets beneath it. Built from the sets alone, never from the graph (F29-Q1). `approach` and `label` are contributor text: untrusted. The result of the list_sufficient_sets tool (F27-T2, R9; D-25, D-28 v3.40): a target's routes, each merged decomposition with its holes' facts aggregated, and its sufficient sets, each a set of statements whose proofs with the closing proofs of its assemblies would close the root; derived by opn_gate.routes.read from targets/<id>/graph.json at main and the served frontier.json, in the record's order: nothing is ranked (D-25). Every value is an id, a count, an enum or a frontier timestamp, so nothing is demarcated. Or an error result naming the source that did not answer, or the arguments refused (R10).

read_at.description: The commit of main the graph was read at, or the branch name when the service could not learn its head (F05-T13).

at_proved.description: What was done at a proved statement: stop (a closed member) or follow (what its proof rests on listed beneath it).

truncated.description: The enumeration reached the service's cap (OPN_API_ROUTES_MAX_SETS).

id.description: <node>@<k>: the node's k-th merged decomposition in the record's order.

approach.description: The route's one-line approach: the partial's `-- approach:` line; for a partial merged before v3.44, what was read from its leading comment or its annex; null when none (F29-R4). Contributor text, untrusted.

live.description: Resolved, and no hole refuted, defective, abandoned or superseded.

name.description: The hole's name in the partial.

label.description: The label graph.json gives the hole's node (its gloss's, else the hole's name, else the target's title, else the id; F29-R3); null when the hole names no node or the product predates v3.44. Contributor text, untrusted.

node.description: The node the hole became, read through revisions; null when the record does not say and F27-R2 could not assign one.

status.description: The node's derived status as graph.json carries it; null when the hole names no node.

attempts.description: The frontier entry's attempt count; null when the node is not on the frontier.

routes.description: How many routes of its own the hole's node has.

attempts.description: Attempts recorded on the route's open holes the frontier lists.

unattempted.description: Open holes the frontier lists with no attempt.

oldest_open_since.description: The earliest ready_since among the route's open holes; null when none is ready.

id.description: s- and ten hex digits of the sha256 of the set's statements and assemblies.

assemblies.description: Interior nodes the set's routes pass through, each still needing its closing proof (D-12 v3.19).

routes.description: The routes the set uses, the root's first.

proof_routes.description: Under at_proved: follow, the routes the proofs of its proved statements went through; empty under stop.

variant.description: The resolves or refutes variant the set goes through, or null.

shared.description: How many of its statements another set also holds.

settles.description: Which way the set settles the root: proves (the root's own routes, its direct proof or a resolves variant) or refutes (a set closing a refutes variant, D-30 v3.46).

closable.description: F28 (draft decisions v3.41): the nodes whose proof exists in parts, in the record's order: each with the link that would close it (a route or, at the root, a resolves variant), that link's inputs, and whether every input is proved (ready) or one is itself closable. A closable node is still open until its closing proof merges.

selector.description: The selector tree over `sets` (F29-R6): the top node has route null and counts every set; a leaf (set non-null) is one of `sets` by id, in their order; an interior node names in `node` the statement its children choose a route on and in each child's `route` the route chosen (null for a child that passes through no route of that statement: it is proved or taken directly on that set's path). Select an interior node to take every set beneath it, a leaf for one. D-25 v3.46: with sets of both sides the top node is a fork whose two children carry `side` (proves, then refutes); select one to take every set of that side.

oneOf.description: The plain path did not answer, or the arguments were refused (F09-R10)

route.description: The route this branch chose (<node>@<k>), null at the top and for a branch that passes through no route of the statement split on.

node.description: The statement the children choose a route on; null at a leaf, at a family whose members differ in no route choice, and at the fork on the side (D-25 v3.46).

set.description: At a leaf, the id of the one set it is; null elsewhere.

sets.description: How many sets this node covers: 1 at a leaf.

side.description: On the two children of the fork the tree opens on when sets of both sides exist: proves (first) or refutes (second); null on every other node, and everywhere when one side only.
